name: Museum Kitzbühel
kurzbeschreibung: The Museum Kitzbühel at Hinterstadt 32 showcases over 60 original paintings by Alfons Walde, 3,000 years of mining history, and scenic rooftop views.
oeffnungszeiten: Summer daily 10:00–17:00 (Thu until 20:00); winter Tue–Sun 14:00–18:00 (Sat from 10:00); off-season hours apply
beschreibung:
Overview

The prestigious Museum Kitzbühel – Alfons Walde Collection is situated at Hinterstadt 32 in the heritage-protected heart of the world-renowned alpine resort town of Kitzbühel. Housed in the town's historic former granary building and an integrated medieval defense tower, the museum stands as the cultural centerpiece of the community. The charming architectural ensemble fascinates art enthusiasts, cultural travelers, and sports historians alike, recognized among the foremost regional museums in Tyrol. Across multiple floors, the museum unites iconic masterpieces of Tyrolean modernism with long-standing regional mining heritage and the town's evolution into a premier winter sports destination. The stellar collection ranks among Western Austria's most acclaimed cultural institutions, inspiring art lovers from around the globe.

Route & Requirements

The historic stone building dates back to the 16th century and was originally constructed as a municipal grain storehouse. The undisputed highlight of the collection is the world's largest permanent retrospective devoted to Kitzbühel painter and architect Alfons Walde (1891–1958). The upper gallery exhibits over 60 original oil paintings alongside roughly 100 drawings, sketches, and iconic vintage tourism posters. Walde's luminous alpine snowfields and dynamic ski figures defined the visual aesthetic of winter in the Alps. Another key exhibition area highlights 3,000 years of regional mining history, tracing prehistoric Bronze Age copper smelting through medieval silver extraction. Furthermore, the museum chronicles the history of alpine ski racing from early Hahnenkamm competitions to the legendary Miracle Team led by Toni Sailer, showcasing vintage racing skis, trophies, and archival footage. Special rotating exhibitions regularly feature regional history, alpine photography, and contemporary fine art.

Visit & Arrival

The museum is open year-round with seasonal hours: summer daily 10:00 to 17:00 (Thursdays late opening until 20:00); winter Tuesday to Sunday 14:00 to 18:00 and Saturdays from 10:00. Admission is €9.00 for adults, free for children and youth under 18. Train travel: ÖBB rail stations Kitzbühel or Hahnenkamm, followed by a five-minute walk through the pedestrian precinct to Hinterstadt 32. By car: B161 to Kitzbühel, parking is available at the Pfarrau car park or the Hahnenkammbahn.

Tips

The entire building is fully wheelchair accessible with an elevator serving all levels. Climbing to the roof terrace atop the medieval defensive tower during summer is a must: visitors enjoy panoramic views of the Streif racecourse and the Kitzbüheler Horn. Relax after your visit in a traditional café in Kitzbühel for fresh homemade pastries. Combine your museum visit with a shopping stroll through the historic town center.
